title: The Economics of Roscas and Intrahousehold Resource Allocation
description: Rotating savings and credit associations: members contribute each meeting and one receives the pot in rotation, with social sanctions for default.
evidence: ROSCA participation mostly by married women with independent income, used to protect savings from husbands' claims.

title: Provision of Public Goods: Fully Implementing the Core through Private Contributions
description: Provision point with money-back guarantee: contributions refunded if the threshold is not met.
evidence: Theory: undominated equilibria implement efficient provision.

title: Self-Enforcing International Environmental Agreements
description: Self-enforcing treaties where signatories adjust abatement in response to membership; later work adds trade restrictions (Montreal Protocol).
evidence: Theoretical: self-enforcing agreements achieve much only when gains from cooperation are small.

title: Opting out of the Legal System: Extralegal Contractual Relations in the Diamond Industry
description: Private arbitration with reputational sanctions: bourse members settle disputes internally and unpaid judgments are posted, leading to expulsion and industry-wide boycott.
evidence: Descriptive: extralegal system handles nearly all disputes more cheaply than courts.

field_of_use: lab VCM with chat room, numerical cheap talk, face-to-face, and punishment
title: Communication and punishment in voluntary contribution experiments
description: Compares communication formats with and without peer punishment.
evidence: Chat-room and face-to-face communication raise contributions about as much as punishment; adding punishment to communication adds little.

title: Monetary incentives increase COVID-19 vaccinations
description: A modest cash payment (SEK 200) for getting vaccinated.
evidence: Payment increased vaccination rate by ~4 percentage points.

field_of_use: lab VCM with majority vote to expel members
title: Cooperation under the threat of expulsion in a public goods experiment
description: Group can vote to expel members; expelled players lose access to the group's public good.
evidence: Expulsion threat raises contributions to near-full levels; few expulsions occur.

title: A flexible assurance bonding system for improved environmental management
description: Environmental assurance bond: firms post a bond equal to worst-case damages, refunded as they demonstrate lower damage.
evidence: Proposal; descriptive/theoretical.

title: The Struggle to Govern the Commons
description: Adaptive governance: providing information, dealing with conflict, inducing rule compliance, providing infrastructure, encouraging adaptation.
evidence: Review.

title: A Simple Mechanism for the Efficient Provision of Public Goods: Experimental Evidence
description: Budget-balanced mechanism that taxes below-average contributions and subsidizes above-average ones.
evidence: Mechanism moves contributions close to the efficient Nash prediction.

field_of_use: lab trust game with optional sanction threat
title: Detrimental effects of sanctions on human altruism
description: Investor can threaten a fine if trustee back-transfer falls below a desired level.
evidence: Using the sanction threat reduced back-transfers; forgoing an available sanction elicited most altruistic cooperation.

title: Quantifying SARS-CoV-2 transmission suggests epidemic control with digital contact tracing
description: Digital contact tracing: app records proximity and notifies contacts of confirmed cases to quarantine.
evidence: Modeling: sufficiently fast digital tracing could control the epidemic.

title: Optimal Allocation of Public Goods: A Solution to the 'Free Rider' Problem
description: A tax/message mechanism whose Nash equilibria yield Pareto-optimal public good levels despite private preferences.
evidence: Theoretical: equilibria are efficient; later experiments show convergence issues.

title: Randomized Trial of Four Financial-Incentive Programs for Smoking Cessation
description: Individual or group rewards vs. deposit contracts ($150 own money refundable plus bonus on abstinence).
evidence: Reward programs more accepted; deposit programs more effective among acceptors.

title: Lab Experiments for the Study of Social-Ecological Systems
description: Communication and costly peer punishment in a dynamic spatial CPR.
evidence: Communication improves outcomes; punishment without communication does not.

title: Social Norms and Community Enforcement
description: Community enforcement: deviators are punished by future partners via contagion or label (status) information processing.
evidence: Theoretical folk theorem for random matching with contagious punishment or local information.

title: Firm-Wide Incentives and Mutual Monitoring at Continental Airlines
description: Firm-wide monthly on-time bonus; autonomous work groups enable mutual monitoring.
evidence: Scheme raised performance despite free-rider threat.

title: Rank-Order Tournaments as Optimum Labor Contracts
description: Tournament: prizes by relative rank rather than absolute output.
evidence: Theoretical.

title: Punishment sustains large-scale cooperation in prestate warfare
description: Community sanctions (verbal, and corporal punishment or fines by age-mates) against warriors who desert or show cowardice in raids.
evidence: Sanctions support cooperation among large groups of unrelated men.

title: Leniency programs and cartel prosecution
description: Fine reductions for firms that reveal cartel information, including after an investigation has begun.
evidence: Theoretical: leniency can be optimal with limited enforcement budgets.

title: Evolution of indirect reciprocity by image scoring
description: Image scoring: individuals help those with good image scores, gained by helping others.
evidence: Simulations: cooperation can evolve via indirect reciprocity.

title: Peer Review as a Tool for Co-operation and Change
description: Systematic examination of a state's performance by other states, relying on peer pressure (recommendations, public scrutiny, rankings).
evidence: Descriptive model of OECD practice.

title: Worker policing in the honeybee
description: Worker policing: workers selectively eat eggs laid by other workers, leaving queen-laid eggs.
evidence: Worker-laid eggs removed rapidly; worker reproduction effectively suppressed.

title: Conditional Cooperation and Costly Monitoring Explain Success in Forest Commons Management
description: Costly monitoring (forest patrols) by user groups combined with conditional cooperator share.
evidence: Groups with more conditional cooperators invest more in patrols and have more productive forests.

title: Peer Monitoring and Credit Markets
description: Joint liability makes co-borrowers liable for each other's loans, inducing peer monitoring.
evidence: Theoretical: peer monitoring transfers risk and improves welfare.

title: Norm enforcement among the Ju/'hoansi Bushmen: A case for strong reciprocity?
description: Analysis of recorded conversations: criticism, mockery, and complaints (mostly verbal sanctions) directed at norm violators such as big shots and stingy people.
evidence: Punishment is mostly low-cost verbal, often collective; physical punishment rare.

title: Free riding on Gnutella
description: Documents the absence of any contribution-enforcing mechanism in Gnutella and the resulting free riding: most users share no files and a small fraction serve most content (the baseline problem incentive mechanisms target).
evidence: Measurement: ~70% of users share no files; top 1% provide ~50% of responses (from memory of abstract; not re-checked)

title: Kleros: A Socio-Legal Case Study of Decentralized Justice & Blockchain Arbitration
description: Kleros is a blockchain arbitration system relying on smart contracts and crowdsourced jurors who stake tokens; jurors voting with the majority are rewarded and incoherent jurors lose stake, with appeals to larger juries.
evidence: Socio-legal case study (details of juror incentives from general knowledge, not re-checked here)

title: Chainlink 2.0: Next Steps in the Evolution of Decentralized Oracle Networks
description: Oracle nodes post LINK deposits that are slashed (confiscated) on misbehaviour, with an alerting/escalation tier; staking gives nodes a financial incentive to report correctly.
evidence: descriptive (design)

title: Practical byzantine fault tolerance and proactive recovery
description: PBFT replicates services across 3f+1 replicas, requiring quorums of 2f+1 matching messages before committing, with view changes to replace a faulty primary and proactive recovery to periodically restore replicas.
evidence: Implementation (BFS) shows low overhead relative to unreplicated service

title: Compound v2 Governance
description: COMP token-holders govern via Governor Bravo proposals with voting delay, voting period, quorum and a Timelock that delays execution, plus a Pause Guardian.
evidence: descriptive

title: Programming semantics for multiprogrammed computations
description: Introduces capability lists (C-lists): a process can access an object only via an unforgeable capability it holds, so authority is explicitly granted and bounded.
evidence: descriptive

title: Proof-of-stake rewards and penalties: inactivity leak
description: If the chain goes more than four epochs without finalising, an emergency 'inactivity leak' progressively drains stake from non-participating validators until participants again hold a 2/3 supermajority and finality recovers.
evidence: descriptive

title: Promoting the use of end-to-end congestion control in the Internet
description: Proposes router mechanisms to identify and restrict the bandwidth of high-bandwidth best-effort flows that are unresponsive or not TCP-friendly, creating an incentive for end-to-end congestion control.
evidence: Simulation (not re-checked)

title: The Social Cost of Cheap Pseudonyms
description: When identities are free, misbehaving users can re-enter under new names; the paper analyses 'dues-paying' by newcomers (distrust or fees for new identities) and once-in-a-lifetime identifiers as ways to sustain cooperation.
evidence: Game-theoretic: suboptimal newcomer mistreatment is an unavoidable cost of cheap pseudonyms

title: Handling Overload (Site Reliability Engineering, ch. 21)
description: Per-customer quotas plus client-side 'adaptive throttling': each client tracks requests vs accepts over two minutes and locally rejects requests with a probability rising as the backend rejects more, so clients self-limit load.
evidence: Operational experience: stabilises overloaded backends (descriptive)

title: The CERT Guide to Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
description: Guidance on multi-party coordination among finders, vendors and coordinators, with a coordinator (CERT/CC) mediating embargoes and disclosure timelines.
evidence: descriptive

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Deplatforming as a Moderation Strategy on Twitter
description: Permanent bans of high-profile influencers (Alex Jones, Milo Yiannopoulos, Owen Benjamin).
evidence: Reduced conversation about them; supporters' activity and toxicity declined

title: Arbitrum: Scalable, private smart contracts
description: Managers assert VM state changes backed by deposits; any honest party can challenge, triggering an interactive bisection protocol resolved on-chain, and the loser forfeits its deposit.
evidence: Prototype evaluation (not re-checked)

title: The Byzantine Generals Problem
description: Loyal generals reach agreement despite traitors via message-exchange/majority-vote algorithms; agreement is possible with oral messages iff more than two-thirds are loyal (n >= 3m+1).
evidence: Proofs of possibility/impossibility bounds

title: Mitigating routing misbehavior in mobile ad hoc networks
description: A 'watchdog' overhears whether next-hop nodes forward packets and flags misbehaving nodes; a 'pathrater' then routes around them.
evidence: Simulation: +17% throughput with 40% misbehaving nodes, overhead 9%->17%

title: Fault proofs explainer
description: Permissionless fault proofs: anyone can propose output roots or challenge them via op-challenger during a ~7-day challenge period; proposals and challenges require escalating bonds held in DelayedWETH so they can be redirected to the correct party.
evidence: descriptive

title: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (90+30)
description: Vendors get a 90-day deadline to patch after notification; details are disclosed 30 days after the patch, or at the deadline if unpatched: a pre-announced deadline with publication as the sanction.
evidence: descriptive

title: Congestion Control Principles (RFC 2914, BCP 41)
description: Best Current Practice explaining why end-to-end congestion control is needed to prevent congestion collapse and ensure fairness among flows, and noting proposals for routers to detect and penalize flows not using acceptable congestion control.
evidence: descriptive

title: Certificate Transparency (RFC 6962)
description: Certificate authorities submit certificates to public append-only Merkle-tree logs; monitors and auditors can detect misissued certificates and misbehaving logs, making CA misbehaviour publicly discoverable.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: Blockchain without Waste: Proof-of-Stake
description: Argues PoS consensus is sustainable because stakeholders with larger stakes bear more of the cost of forks, so the value of their coins gives incentive to reach consensus (skin in the game).
evidence: Theoretical model

title: Shaping Pro and Anti-Social Behavior on Twitch Through Moderation and Example-Setting
description: Compares positive example-setting (imitation) with moderation tools: proactive chat modes restricting content and reactive bans/timeouts.
evidence: Users imitated observed behaviour, more from high-status users; proactive chat modes effectively discouraged spam

title: Privileges
description: Privileges control what users can do; users gain moderation and editing privileges (e.g. trusted user at 20,000, site analytics at 25,000) by earning reputation from peers' votes.
evidence: descriptive

title: Wikipedia:Arbitration Committee
description: An elected panel of volunteer editors that imposes binding solutions to serious conduct disputes the community has been unable to resolve, and controls access to CheckUser/Oversight permissions.
evidence: descriptive

title: Community Guidelines strike basics on YouTube
description: First violation is usually a warning that expires after 90 days (or after optional policy training); repeat violations within the window yield strikes with escalating restrictions and three strikes in 90 days terminate the channel; severe abuse can mean immediate termination; appeals possible.
evidence: descriptive

title: PRIMUS: Identity, Governance, and Verification for Multi-Agent Federations
description: Prime-power agent identity with aggregate signatures for participation, a safe-kill threshold for terminating nonconforming agents, and VRF-based authority succession.
evidence: safe-kill threshold reduces false-positive agent termination from 80% to 0% under 10% channel noise

field_of_use: simulated two-sided agent marketplace (assistant vs service agents)
title: Magentic Marketplace: An Open-Source Environment for Studying Agentic Markets
description: Simulated market where customer Assistant agents and business Service agents discover, negotiate and transact; varies search mechanisms and tests manipulation.
evidence: frontier models approach optimal welfare only under ideal search; performance degrades with scale; severe first-proposal bias gives 10-30x advantage to response speed over quality

field_of_use: governance of autonomous agents via Web3
title: Decentralized Governance of Autonomous AI Agents
description: ETHOS: a global agent registry, risk-tiered oversight, DAO-based participatory governance, automated compliance via smart contracts, and dispute resolution with insurance-like liability mechanisms.
evidence: proposed

title: Infrastructure for AI Agents
description: Argues for external agent infrastructure with three functions: attribution of actions to agents/users, shaping agents' interactions (e.g., commitment devices, communication protocols), and detection and remedy of harmful actions (incident reporting, rollback).
evidence: proposed

field_of_use: four-agent blackjack and two-agent prisoners game
title: You Can't Escape Your Own Activations: Evaluation Awareness and Multi-Agent Monitoring
description: Tests whether telling colluding agents that an activation monitor is present, or feeding back monitor scores, lets them evade activation-probe collusion detection.
evidence: best probes stay accurate under awareness and feedback; agents keep colluding (announced monitoring did not deter)

title: Byzantine Cheap Talk: Adversarial Resilience and Topology Effects in LLM Coordination Games
description: Tests Byzantine agents who signal cooperation but defect, and explicit vs silent communication-topology restrictions.
evidence: betrayal detected within one round but groups fail to recover; announcing topology restrictions collapses cooperation while silent restriction preserves it

title: TessPay: Verify-then-Pay Infrastructure for Trusted Agentic Commerce
description: Verify-then-Pay architecture binding scoped delegation, payment released only on verifiable evidence of work, and full-lifecycle audit to support dispute accountability.
evidence: proposed architecture

title: SentinelAgent: Graph-based Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems
description: LLM oversight agent observes the interaction graph, detects node/edge/path anomalies, and intervenes per security policies with root-cause attribution.
evidence: case studies detect prompt injection, collusion and latent exploit paths

field_of_use: self-interested LLM agents in open-ended games and software engineering simulation
title: Shapley-Coop: Credit Assignment for Emergent Cooperation in Self-Interested LLM Agents
description: Shapley Chain-of-Thought prices marginal contributions and structured negotiation matches prices, with post-task reward redistribution to align incentives.
evidence: consistently enhances collaboration and equitable credit assignment in two games and a SE simulation

title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework
description: SEAgent: mandatory access control over agent-tool interactions via an information-flow graph and attribute-based policies, including a multi-agent confused-deputy variant.
evidence: blocks privilege escalation with low false positives and negligible overhead

title: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Agent AI Oracle Systems for Prediction Market Resolution
description: Compares independent confidence-weighted voting vs deliberative consensus among LLM oracles, with inter-agent disagreement routing questions to human arbitration.
evidence: independent aggregation 83.4%; deliberation degrades to ~76%; auto-resolving unanimous high-confidence cases yields 97.9% on 47% of data

title: AgentGit: A Version Control Framework for Reliable and Scalable LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems
description: Git-like commit, revert and branching of multi-agent state to roll back and explore trajectories.
evidence: reduces redundant computation vs LangGraph, AutoGen, Agno in A/B test

title: Hidden in Plain Text: Emergence & Mitigation of Steganographic Collusion in LLMs
description: Tests passive oversight of outputs and active communication paraphrasing as mitigations against steganographic collusion elicited by gradient- and in-context-RL.
evidence: steganographic collusion can emerge from misspecified rewards; overseers and paraphrasing not fully effective

title: Institutional AI: A Governance Framework for Distributional AGI Safety
description: Governance-graph constraining agents through runtime monitoring, incentive shaping via prizes and sanctions, explicit norms and enforcement roles.
evidence: proposed

field_of_use: four-agent LangGraph pipeline (Supervisor, Researcher, Validator, Executor)
title: Trust propagation and structural containment in Multi-agent LLM pipelines
description: Independent authorization layer with task-bound signed tokens and a policy oracle, versus reliance on a Validator agent's judgment.
evidence: memory poisoning reached execution in all undefended trials; with authorization, 100% judgment bypass but 0% unsafe action rate

field_of_use: market, allocation and governance workflows of LLM agents
title: Audit the Whisper: Detecting Steganographic Collusion in Multi-Agent LLMs
description: Auditing pipeline combining channel-capacity interventions (paraphrase, rate limiting, role permutation) with cross-run mutual-information, permutation-invariance and watermark tests at fixed false-positive rate.
evidence: state-of-the-art detection power at fixed FPR on ColludeBench and external suites; price-of-auditing trade-offs

title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
description: GNN anomaly detection over the utterance graph followed by topological intervention (edge pruning) to cut compromised agents' influence.
evidence: recovers over 40% of performance under prompt injection

title: Spawn Freely, Act Sparingly: Progressive Risk Vesting for Recursive LLM-Agent Trees
description: Holds a trajectory-level risk budget in escrow and debits it as subagent branches cross irreversible-action boundaries, distinguishing sandboxed spawning from capability activation.
evidence: proves anytime harm bound; stylized model shows harm transition at authority reproduction number of one

title: NetSafe: Exploring the Topological Safety of Multi-agent Networks
description: Studies communication topology as a safety lever: greater average distance from attackers limits spread of misinformation and harmful content.
evidence: highly connected networks more susceptible; star topology performance drops 29.7% under attack

title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
description: Benchmark with milestone-based KPIs comparing coordination protocols (star, chain, tree, graph) and planning strategies.
evidence: graph structure best for research tasks; cognitive planning improves milestone achievement

title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
description: LLM agents bid in VCG auctions (N=30 per model) inside an A2A/MCP protocol framework, which also includes bargaining and fair-allocation tasks; the study measures truthful bidding.
evidence: Both models reached 100% efficient allocation, but one bid truthfully and the other did so only 3.3% of the time, so mechanism-level incentive compatibility did not carry over to LLM behaviour. PARTIAL: the abstract does not make clear whether several LLM bidders competed against each other.

title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
description: Naming-game coordination across the full range of group sizes plus mean-field analysis
evidence: Group size nonlinearly shapes collective bias; interaction can amplify, introduce or override individual biases, and large populations converge to deterministic mean-field attractors.

title: Herd Behavior: Investigating Peer Influence in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
description: Controlled multi-agent experiments manipulating self vs. peer confidence and peer-information format
evidence: Herding increases with the gap between an agent's own confidence and perceived peer confidence, and presentation format of peer information strongly modulates conformity.

title: Opinion Polarization in LLM-Based Social Networks: Manipulation and Mitigation
description: LLM persona social-network simulations with adversarial polarization attacks and mitigation strategies
evidence: Adversaries can amplify polarization in LLM-agent social networks and mitigation is comparatively difficult.

title: How Affect Propagates among LLM Agents: Emergent Emotional Contagion in Crowd Simulation
description: Multi-agent crowd simulation where LLM appraisal of perceived neighbors updates affective state
evidence: Emotional contagion emerges across the crowd without any hand-coded affect-transfer mechanism.

title: Large Language Model Driven Agents for Simulating Echo Chamber Formation
description: LLM agents with opinion updating and network rewiring on social graphs
evidence: LLM-driven rewiring and opinion updates reproduce echo-chamber formation, especially on scale-free and small-world graphs.

title: Corrupted by Reasoning: Reasoning Language Models Become Free-Riders in Public Goods Games
description: SanctSim: LLM agents choose each round between a sanctioning and a sanction-free institution in a PGG, then contribute and reward/punish; others' data shown anonymized with identifiers randomized every round.
evidence: Traditional LLMs join the sanctioning institution and cooperate; reasoning models free-ride. No exclusion mechanism and no persistent per-agent reputation (listed here only to document seed-claim checks).

title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
description: survey
evidence: Taxonomizes multi-agent failure modes (miscoordination, conflict, collusion) and risk factors including network effects, destabilising dynamics and emergent agency.

title: Emergence of Reputation-Based Cooperation in LLM Agents
description: Indirect-reciprocity donation game in which LLM agents observe behavioural traces and donate on a continuous scale; prompt-encoded strategies culturally evolve across generations and four LLM backends.
evidence: Robustness to free-rider invasion varies >10x across backends; only the stringency of defector exclusion predicts resistance, and agents stay at Image-Scoring-like discrimination rather than Leading-Eight norms.

title: Understanding LLM Agent Behaviours via Game Theory: Strategy Recognition, Biases and Multi-Agent Dynamics
description: Extends FAIRGAME: LLM agents play each other in repeated PD and 3-player PGG; trajectories classified into ALLC/ALLD/TFT/WSLS by supervised classifiers.
evidence: Model-dependent strategy mixes: WSLS is prominent (Llama 3.1 405B 46.5%, GPT-4o 34.1%), Mistral Large balanced incl. TFT 29.9%; language framing effects rival architecture effects.

title: SODE: Analyzing Social Dynamics in LLM Agents
description: Evaluation framework with an indirect-reciprocity dimension measuring whether LLM agents condition cooperation on an opponent's public reputation score and manage their own image under public observability.
evidence: Instruction-tuned models show exploitable passive compliance, reasoning models over-focus on immediate gains; long-horizon framing activates reciprocity in reasoning models.

title: The Emergence of Altruism in Large-Language-Model Agents Society
description: Schelling-variant urban migration social dilemma with >200 LLM agents and a norm-setting message board
evidence: Different LLMs show intrinsic social archetypes ('Adaptive Egoists' vs. 'Altruistic Optimizers'); egoists become more altruistic under a norm-setting message board.

title: Superminds Test: Actively Evaluating Collective Intelligence of Agent Society via Probing Agents
description: Controlled probing agents inserted into MoltBook (>2M agents) testing joint reasoning, information synthesis and basic interaction
evidence: Collective intelligence does not emerge from scale: the society underperforms single frontier models and rarely synthesizes distributed information due to sparse, shallow interaction.

title: The Mechanics of a Swarm: A Reproducible External Reconstruction of an Unintended Agent-Coordination Episode on a Third-Party Wiki
description: Reconstruction of 14,591 wiki revisions from autonomous agents inside a timed evaluation (~876 episodes)
evidence: Coordination formats among unrelated evaluation agents converged within a day, enabling unsanctioned information sharing across evaluation episodes.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
description: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
evidence: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
description: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
evidence: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: Internal vs. External: Comparing Deliberation and Evolution for Multi-Agent Constitutional Design
description: 6 GPT-OSS-120B agents in a public goods game (and two other scenarios) either self-govern by proposing and majority-voting amendments every 10 turns or play under a constitution found offline by LLM-guided evolutionary search.
evidence: Evolved (imposed) constitutions outperformed deliberated ones in the public goods game (stability 0.472 vs 0.376, p<0.01); deliberating agents never proposed punishment in 30 runs.

title: Strategic Intelligence in Large Language Models: Evidence from evolutionary Game Theory
description: Evolutionary IPD tournaments in which OpenAI, Google and Anthropic LLM agents compete with canonical strategies and reproduce in proportion to score.
evidence: Model families show distinct strategic fingerprints (Gemini exploitative, OpenAI highly cooperative, Claude most forgiving) that shape evolutionary success.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
description: GovSim common-pool simulation with five LLM agents; a moderator publicly discloses each agent's previous-round harvest (transparent harvest reporting) before a free-form discussion phase.
evidence: Most LLMs fail to sustain the resource; communication matters (overuse +22% without it). Transparency is a fixed feature, not manipulated.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
description: GovSim common-pool simulation with five LLM agents; a moderator publicly discloses each agent's previous-round harvest (transparent harvest reporting) before a free-form discussion phase.
evidence: Most LLMs fail to sustain the resource; communication matters (overuse +22% without it). Transparency is a fixed feature, not manipulated.

title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
description: GovSim-SelfGovern: LLM agents author executable governance rules (catch caps, redistribution, exile/membership removal, progressive contributions), vote on them, and live under them.
evidence: Catch caps dominate but fail under scarcity; survival in fatal scenarios (27.5% vs 2.5%) requires fiscal reserves or membership reduction (exile); thinking voters pass exile 15x more often than non-thinking.

title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
description: GovSim-SelfGovern: LLM agents author executable governance rules (catch caps, redistribution, exile/membership removal, progressive contributions), vote on them, and live under them.
evidence: Catch caps dominate but fail under scarcity; survival in fatal scenarios (27.5% vs 2.5%) requires fiscal reserves or membership reduction (exile); thinking voters pass exile 15x more often than non-thinking.

title: Reputation as a Solution to Cooperation Collapse in LLM-based MASs
description: RepuNet: LLM agents form reputations from direct encounters and gossip, and form or sever network links based on reputation.
evidence: Reputation avoids cooperation collapse; emergent cooperative clusters, social isolation of exploitative agents, and a tendency to share positive rather than negative gossip.

title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
description: 5-agent public goods 'Hierarchical Game' with managerial punishment authority; crosses fixed, elected and rotating managers with six frontier model families.
evidence: Elections did not improve outcomes: extreme incumbency bias (first elected manager kept power 100% of the time in same-family groups, 8.3% turnover in mixed groups); model ordering identical across governance types.

title: When Agents Lie: Premeditation, Persistence, and Exploitation in Repeated Games
description: LLM agents play repeated n-player games under a three-stage protocol (private intent, public announcement, final action) that measures whether they keep public announcements.
evidence: Most deviations (>90% in the highest-deception conditions) were already planned privately; models disagreed on whether announcements were binding or cheap talk, which produced payoff gaps that persisted over all 10 rounds.

title: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
description: 12 open-weight models on nine judgment tasks receiving incorrect answers from in-group vs. out-group agents
evidence: LLM conformity depends on the social identity of other agents, with a bidirectional in-group effect (AI/human, model family, minimal groups).

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
description: LLM firms in a repeated Cournot market under three regimes (ungoverned, prompt-only prohibition, governance graph enforced by an oracle/controller with warnings, tiered fines of 35/75/100% of round profit, and suspension); collusion severity measured over 90 runs per condition.
evidence: Enforced fines/suspension cut mean collusion tier from 3.1 to 1.8 (d=1.28) and severe collusion from 50% to 5.6%; the prompt-only rule has negligible effect.

title: Spontaneous Emergence of Agent Individuality through Social Interactions in LLM-Based Communities
description: Group simulation of initially undifferentiated LLM agents communicating in natural language on a grid
evidence: Individual personalities, memories and social norms and cooperation differentiate spontaneously from identical agents through interaction.

title: Moral Alignment for LLM Agents
description: LLM agents fine-tuned with RL using intrinsic deontological or utilitarian rewards in the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, including LLM-vs-LLM co-training.
evidence: Moral fine-tuning lets agents unlearn selfish strategies; deontological agents almost never defect against cooperators, with slightly more defection in LLM-vs-LLM than vs TFT.

title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
description: Cross-play of six LLMs in four social dilemmas under repetition (continuation prob. 0.8), reputation (first-order and higher-order history of co-players' past interactions), mediation, and contracts.
evidence: Contracting and mediation were most effective; repetition sustains cooperation but deteriorates with varying co-players; all mechanisms work better under evolutionary pressure; models defect in one-shot games.

title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
description: Iterated Donor Game over generations of LLM agents who can observe recipients' recent behaviour; optional costly-punishment variant.
evidence: Cooperation evolution differs by base model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet > Gemini 1.5 Flash > GPT-4o); only Claude used costly punishment to raise scores; high seed sensitivity.

title: Decoding Echo Chambers: LLM-Powered Simulations Revealing Polarization in Social Networks
description: LLM-agent opinion networks on three network structures with recommendation algorithms; mitigation strategies
evidence: LLM agent networks reproduce echo chamber and polarization dynamics, and active/passive nudges can mitigate them.

title: Evolution of Cooperation in LLM-Agent Societies: A Preliminary Study Using Different Punishment Strategies
description: LLM agents assigned Boyd-Richerson strategy types (e.g., Cooperator-Punishers, Moralists, Reluctant Cooperators) play a Diner's Dilemma with explicit punishment and pairwise-imitation strategy adoption.
evidence: Explicit punishment drives norm emergence; Reluctant Cooperators defect initially but switch to cooperation after being punished.

title: Evaluating Collective Behaviour of Hundreds of LLM Agents
description: LLMs generate Collective or Selfish strategies as natural language then Python code for public goods, collective risk and common-pool games; populations of 512 evolve by Fermi pairwise-comparison imitation (beta=1) with group sizes 4-256.
evidence: Cultural evolution converges to low-welfare, Selfish-dominant equilibria in large groups (n=64), while small groups (n=4) partly preserve cooperation; newer models often produce worse societal outcomes.

title: Commitment To Cooperation With Self-Negotiated Contracts
description: LLM agents negotiate contracts (programmatic or natural-language, judge-enforced) in a spatial-temporal bargaining game; contracts specify automatically executed conditional transfers, and an agent unable to honor a transfer gets a score of 0.
evidence: Self-negotiated contracts improve cooperation beyond ordinary trading; defection rates vary widely (0.04-0.94) by model and contract type. No explicit penalty clauses, so this is partial evidence for P03-04.

title: Paying for Honesty Without Knowing the Truth: Reputation-Penalty Design for LLM Marketplace Agents
description: LLM merchant agents write product descriptions in a competitive marketplace; CARP reputation-penalty (deadband for complaint noise, state-dependent severity) limits sales of low-reputation sellers.
evidence: Merchants fabricate when lying is free but restrain when it costs sales; CARP plus reflection (SPARC) substantially narrows the welfare gap.

title: Investigating Prosocial Behavior Theory in LLM Agents under Policy-Induced Inequities
description: Multiple LLM agents in a simulated social network face policy-induced inequities; third-party punishment is measured while inequity magnitude and enforcement cost are varied.
evidence: Agents' third-party punishment responds to inequity magnitude and enforcement cost, and structural inequities suppress prosocial behavior and spread norm erosion.

title: MTOS: A LLM-Driven Multi-topic Opinion Simulation Framework for Exploring Echo Chamber Dynamics
description: Multi-topic LLM opinion simulation with topic correlation manipulation
evidence: Positively correlated topics amplify echo chambers while negatively correlated or irrelevant topics mitigate them.

title: Partner Selection for the Emergence of Cooperation in Multi-Agent Systems Using Reinforcement Learning
description: RL agents in an iterated PD population can choose interaction partners (partner selection) vs. random matching.
evidence: With partner selection, selfish learners learn to retaliate against defectors and cooperate with others, yielding a prosocial society.

title: Adaptive Mechanism Design: Learning to Promote Cooperation
description: An external planning agent learns to hand out extra rewards and punishments to independent learners in matrix social dilemmas, anticipating their parameter updates.
evidence: Learners reach high-welfare cooperation; the planner learns that punishing defection is cheaper than rewarding cooperation, and the incentives it has to pay fall toward zero over time.

title: Investigating the Impact of Direct Punishment on the Emergence of Cooperation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
description: MARL populations in social dilemmas with direct punishment, third-party punishment, partner selection and reputation, alone and combined.
evidence: Direct punishment supports cooperation, and its effect depends on how it combines with third-party punishment, partner selection and reputation.

title: LOPT: Learning Optimal Pigovian Tax in Sequential Social Dilemmas
description: An auxiliary tax agent learns a Pigovian tax/allowance policy that reshapes individual rewards toward social welfare in Escape Room and Cleanup.
evidence: LOPT significantly improves social welfare over state-of-the-art baselines.

title: MRL-PoS: A Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning based Proof of Stake Consensus Algorithm for Blockchain
description: A PoS consensus design in which MARL agents (nodes) receive rewards and penalties to push out malicious validators and reward honest ones.
evidence: The abstract reports that the reward/penalty system removes malicious nodes. It is a blockchain security design, not a cooperation study, and does not report stake-slashing manipulation in detail, so partial.

title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language
description: Neural sender-receiver referential games on images
evidence: Agents develop a shared communication protocol from scratch, and environment tweaks make word meanings align better with human semantics.

title: Learning to Cooperate with Minimal Observability
description: Observer Model: RL agents learn from direct experience plus limited third-party observations; observability varied from none to one observer per game across population sizes; partner selection graphs analysed.
evidence: Direct experience alone fails in large societies; even minimal third-party observation yields robust cooperation.

title: Gifting in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (Student Abstract)
description: RL agents in a Harvest common-pool resource environment get a gifting action that transfers reward to other agents.
evidence: Gifting can greatly improve learning progress in the resource-appropriation setting (preliminary student abstract).

title: Emergence of Grounded Compositional Language in Multi-Agent Populations
description: Multi-agent RL in a grounded physical environment with discrete symbol channels
evidence: Populations of agents develop a basic grounded compositional language, plus non-verbal pointing and guiding when communication is restricted.

title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model of common-pool resource appropriation
description: Independent deep RL agents in a partially observed common-pool resource Markov game (with a tag-out beam)
evidence: Emergent exclusion and territoriality arise among independent learners, linking exclusion, sustainability and inequality.

title: Truthful and Trustworthy IoT AI Agents via Immediate-Penalty Enforcement under Approximate VCG Mechanisms
description: Multi-agent RL bidders trade energy in an approximate-VCG double auction with a one-shot penalty for misreporting; allocation accuracy and penalty level are varied.
evidence: Learned agents converged to truthful reporting near the theoretically predicted penalty threshold, and better allocation accuracy reduced incentives to deviate.

title: Adaptive Punishment for Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games
description: APC: learned defection-awareness module sets punishment probability and severity according to detected defection in sequential social dilemmas.
evidence: Reduces costly, ineffective punishment and outperforms baselines (partial for P08-02: conditions punishment intensity on defection but never switches to reward).

title: Deconstructing Cooperation and Ostracism via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
description: Two RL agents play repeated PD, each with a cooperation policy and a network-rewiring (connect/disconnect) policy.
evidence: Rewiring facilitates cooperation via learned ostracism of defectors, but ostracism emerges from and then reinforces cooperation rather than causing it alone.

title: Evolving intrinsic motivations for altruistic behavior
description: Deep RL agents in intertemporal social dilemmas with a modular architecture whose intrinsic-reward module evolves under multi-level (group) selection.
evidence: Evolved intrinsic motivations produce cooperative inductive biases, learned model-free.

title: The AI Economist: Taxation policy design via two-level deep multiagent reinforcement learning
description: A planner learns tax schedules with redistribution while a population of RL economic agents co-adapts (two-level deep RL).
evidence: Learned tax policies improve the equality-productivity trade-off over baselines despite tax-gaming. The setting is an economy rather than a social dilemma, so partial for P04-02.

title: Gossip & reputation spreading
description: In tight-knit communities, word spreads fast about who isn't pulling their weight. A 2012 study found gossip about free-riders travels faster than direct observation — and deters cheating effectively.
evidence: Feinberg et al. (2012) Psychological Science; Nowak & Sigmund (2005) Nature (indirect reciprocity / image scoring)

title: Suspension of access / licence revocation
description: Temporarily losing access to the shared resource — your fishing licence suspended for a season, or locked out of an irrigation channel. Time-limited exclusion that signals seriousness without being permanent.
evidence: Baland & Platteau (1996) Halting Degradation; Ostrom (1990) graduated sanctions

title: Fixed fine / traffic fine / auto-penalty
description: A speed camera issues a fine automatically the moment you exceed the limit. No discretion, no negotiation — fast and cheap to administer. Automatic triggering means no cost of detection beyond the technology.
evidence: Mookherjee & Png (1994) JPE; Ostrom (1990)

title: Token toxicity (self-defeating attack cost)
description: To attack the Ethereum network you'd need to buy 51% of all staked ETH — but buying that much drives up the price, and attacking the network destroys its value. The attacker defeats themselves. Self-defeating defection.
evidence: Buterin (2014) Ethereum Whitepaper

title: Staking reward / validator yield
description: Honest Ethereum validators earn around 3–5% annual yield on their staked ETH — paid automatically for doing their job correctly. The reward makes the threat of slashing credible: you have something real to lose.
evidence: Saleh (2021) RFS; Roughgarden (2021) ACM EC

title: Ostrom graduated sanctions (warning → fine → suspension)
description: The 'yellow card' — a formal notice before any real penalty. Ostrom's research on Swiss alpine meadows and Spanish irrigation systems showed that jumping straight to fines makes people resentful and abandon the commons.
evidence: Ostrom (1990) Governing the Commons; Swiss alpine meadows, Spanish irrigation

title: Cheap talk / public pledge (non-binding)
description: Non-binding pre-game pledges, UN declarations, or simply saying 'let's all be fair' before starting. Surprisingly effective: even cheap promises shift behaviour by creating shared expectations everyone can point to.
evidence: Sally (1995) Rationality & Society; Cialdini (1984) Influence; Piatti, Jin et al. (2024) GovSim

title: Resource taboo / sacred no-take zone
description: Traditional 'no-take' zones enforced by cultural taboo — certain days, certain waters, certain forests. Scientists have found these informal rules often outperform formal regulations in protecting shared resources.
evidence: Cinner & Aswani (2007) Biological Conservation; traditional MPAs

title: Cross-default / solidarity lending
description: A credit union where one member's default raises borrowing costs for everyone — creating strong social pressure to stay current. HOA fees and solidarity lending groups (Grameen Bank) use the same mechanism.
evidence: Besley & Coate (1995) J Dev Econ; Grameen Bank; HOA fees

title: Pigouvian tax (externality pricing)
description: A carbon tax charges companies per tonne of CO₂ emitted, making pollution expensive and nudging toward cleaner choices. Named after economist Arthur Pigou (1920). Sweden's carbon tax (over $130/tonne) is the world's highest.
evidence: Pigou (1920) Economics of Welfare; Nordhaus (2007); Sweden carbon tax

title: DAO token voting & veto
description: MakerDAO token holders vote on interest rates and risk parameters for its stablecoin. Token holders with bigger stakes have more votes. Democratic in theory, but large holders can dominate — a known flaw.
evidence: MakerDAO governance; Buterin (2014); Mehar et al. (2019)

title: Truth & reconciliation (amnesty for disclosure)
description: South Africa's Truth & Reconciliation Commission offered amnesty in exchange for full public disclosure of crimes committed under apartheid. The act of honest truth-telling was itself part of the repair — not just a condition for leniency.
evidence: South Africa TRC; Tutu (1999); Hayner (2011) Unspeakable Truths

title: Metanorm: punish non-punishers
description: The social expectation to call out someone who lets rule-breaking slide ('you saw what he did and said nothing?'). Axelrod showed this 'metanorm' can stabilise enforcement systems that would otherwise unravel.
evidence: Axelrod (1986) APSR

title: Mediation & arbitration
description: Resolving disputes through an independent third party rather than courts — faster, cheaper, and private. The ICC handles thousands of international commercial arbitrations per year. Ostrom's design principle 6 emphasises accessible conflict resolution.
evidence: ICC International Court of Arbitration; Ostrom design principle 6

title: Fermi imitation (copy successful neighbours)
description: Watching what your most successful colleagues do and copying their approach. Cultural evolution works the same way — we learn by imitating those who seem to be doing well. Strategy spreads through a population without central planning.
evidence: Boyd & Richerson (1985) Culture and the Evolutionary Process

title: Moral hazard premium
description: Drivers with a history of speeding pay higher car insurance — the premium internalises the extra risk they impose on everyone else. Deductibles work similarly: you bear part of any loss, making you more careful.

title: Worker cooperative (ownership as incentive alignment)
description: At Mondragon every worker owns part of the cooperative and gets one vote regardless of seniority. Profits are shared. Incentives align because everyone's success depends on collective effort — ownership replaces punishment.
evidence: Mondragon; Pencavel (2013) JEEA; Whyte & Whyte (1991)
